sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012)
Panama-Spain Double Taxation Agreement (signed 2010, in force 2012)
Panama-Republic of Korea Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Private Interest Foundations are governed by Law 25 of 12 June 1995 and its implementing regulations of the Public Registry of Panama. AML/CFT obligations derive from Law 23 of 27 April 2015, as amended by Law 70 of 22 June 2017 and Law 67 of 6 November 2020 (creating the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros, SSRF), Decree 46 of 13 May 2016, Cabinet Decree 17 of 10 May 2019, and Executive Decree 52 of 2 September 2020 (central UBO registry and enhanced due diligence resolution framework).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation charter (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado) executed as a public deed before a Panamanian Notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama and Public Registry of Panama
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Dirección General de Certificación y Legalizaciones of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama for foreign use; internal registration does not require foreign legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founder corporate existence and good standing certificate, or notarized passport and bank reference for a natural-person founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or notarial authority of the founder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the state of origin; for non-Hague Convention states, full consular legalization chain through the Panamanian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the foundation council members, protector, and registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of Panama or foreign notary with apostille or consular legalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address for all foundation council members, the protector, and named beneficiaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular certification of notarial attestations plus sworn translator certification in Spanish

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD and enhanced due diligence under Law 23 of 2015 and SSRF rules: screening of the founder, foundation council members, protector, registered agent, and every named beneficiary against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI sanctions, and public designations issued in Panama; automatic re-screening on each payment-rail or beneficiary change; PEP classification (public officials, family members, and close associates) requires senior-management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring; cash-on-delivery collections of USD 10,000 or more per single or linked operation trigger currency-transaction reporting to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero, and any AML/CFT suspicion associated with the ISIC 4791 COD settlement model requires immediate STR filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Online Clearance and Reservation Services (Oficina Virtual, www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Law 25 of 1995 requires the distinctive name to be rendered in Latin script and immediately followed by the statutory suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado' (Private Interest Foundation); the registry processes filings exclusively in Spanish, and any foreign-language word forming part of the name must be transliterated and approved at the pre-clearance stage; names that are identical, phonetically equivalent, or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity are automatically refused.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Bank, Banking and any synonym implying deposit-taking
Seguros, Reaseguros, Insurance or underwriting terminology
Trust, Fideicomiso, Fiduciario or fiduciary-sounding tokens
Financiera, Fondo de Inversión, Mutual Fund terminology
Lotería, Casino, Juegos de Azar and gambling tokens requiring separate licensing
Gobierno, Nacional, República, Ministerio, Policía and other official and sensitive tokens requiring ministerial approval
Cruz Roja, Red Cross and protected humanitarian emblems
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The certificate of name availability is renewable for successive 30-day terms only if a new application is filed before the original reservation lapses; upon statutory refusal the applicant may file a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Director General of the Public Registry within five working days of notification, followed by a hierarchic administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) confirmed within five working days, and ultimately an annulment action before the Third Chamber of Administrative Litigation of the Supreme Court of Justice; a parallel reservation under a new distinct name may be filed without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual and remote operation is permissible for the offshore COD e-commerce activity and payment-rail settlements; however, the foundation must continuously maintain a registered agent and a statutory registered office in Panama, and the AML/CFT file, UBO records, foundation minute book, and accounting records must remain physically accessible at the Panamanian registered office for SSRF, SUGAF, and judicial inspection. A virtual office cannot replace the statutory Panamanian domicile.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-Enhanced. Modeled unannounced on-site inspection probability of approximately 8% per annum in year one, increasing to about 15% when gross annual COD settlements exceed USD 1,000,000, cash remittances exceed 30% of settlement volume, or non-bank rails (Airwallex or local logistics remittance) carry over USD 250,000 per quarter.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory arancel schedule of the Public Registry of Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial formation deed (escritura constitutiva) including USD 10,000 minimum foundation capital verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial arancel in force in Panama; prevailing market benchmark USD 250-350

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration fee for foundation charter in the Public Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff scaled to declared foundation capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SSRF-administered Central UBO Registry through the registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative fee schedule under Cabinet Decree 17 of 2019 and Executive Decree 52 of 2020, approximately USD 100 per entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and statutory registered office, first annual retainer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian law firm or registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for PIF agency services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC file setup, PEP and consolidated sanctions screening for founder, council, protector, and beneficiaries
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent compliance officer and external AML counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per risk file, Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of apostilled foreign corporate and identity documents
Hague apostilles and consular legalization fees for founder jurisdiction documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authorities and Panamanian consulates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory and consular fee schedules of each issuing state

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External counsel pre-incorporation due diligence and constitution drafting fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External corporate and tax counsel admitted to the Panama bar
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat engagement fee for Stage 1 PIF formation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 July 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (Ley Nº 25 de 12 de julio de 1995 sobre Fundaciones de Interés Privado), Articles 1–35, as supplemented by the general regulations of the Public Registry of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) – División de Personas Jurídicas y Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado), submitted for inscription in the Public Registry together with the Foundation Council's organizational minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by Law No. 25 of 1995; standard banking practice requires a declared initial endowment of at least USD 10,000 in the Foundation Charter. No statutory escrow or blocked deposit account is mandated; the endowment must be fully subscribed but may remain under the Foundation's free control.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BY UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE COUNCIL OF THE PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION [FOUNDATION NAME], IT IS RESOLVED: (1) The initial endowment of USD 10,000 is subscribed and fully paid in, without any statutory escrow requirement. (2) The registered office is fixed at [Panama City, Republic of Panama address], and the Resident Agent [AGENT NAME] is ratified as legal representative for service of process. (3) The following officers are appointed, each with authority to act jointly or severally: [NAME] as President, [NAME] as Secretary, and [NAME] as Treasurer, empowered to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and file regulatory returns. (4) The Council authorizes all formation, governance, and licensing steps for ISIC 4791 cash-on-delivery mail-order retail operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Nombre y Certificados, through the online portal 'Registro en Línea' or in-person service windows.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative proposed foundation names with the founder's identification or the registered agent's power of attorney. The registry verifies the absence of identical or confusingly similar names and issues a name reservation certificate upon payment of the fixed tariff.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Certified copy of founder's passport
Notarized power of attorney in favor of the resident agent, legalized as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected or opposed, file the next alternative name on the reserve list; no substantive cure is needed beyond paying the applicable re-filing tariff and submitting a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública accredited by the Supreme Court of Justice of Panama.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legal counsel prepares the Foundation Charter containing the foundation's purposes, endowment, council members, registered office, resident agent designation, and any reserved regulations. The founder or attorney-in-fact appears physically before the notary to execute the deed; the notary protocols the instrument and delivers an authorized first testimonio.
required_dossiers: Foundation Charter draft
Name reservation certificate
Passport copies of founder and council members
Notarized power of attorney if founder is not personally present
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarial pre-review identifies legal defects, counsel redrafts the affected clauses and the execution ceremony is repeated; a new notarial authorization fee is charged, without registry sanction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation Charter in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – División de Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the first notarial testimonio of the Foundation Charter to the Public Registry for legal review and inscription. The registry verifies compliance with Law No. 25 of 1995, records the foundation, and issues the corresponding inscription certificate evidencing legal existence.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy (testimonio) of the Foundation Charter
Proof of payment of registry inscription fees
Certified Spanish translation of any non-Spanish document
Notarized power of attorney authorizing the registered agent to file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry returns observations (vistas), file a corrective brief within five working days, amend the deed clauses as instructed, and pay the resubmission tariff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ratification of Resident Agent and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Resident Agent registered with the Public Registry of Panama; supervision by the Public Registry control section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Foundation Charter designates the resident agent and the registered office address. The resident agent executes a formal acceptance, and the Foundation Council ratifies the designation in an organizational resolution. Any subsequent change is filed with the Public Registry as an amendment.
required_dossiers: Resident agent acceptance letter
Consent letter from the registered office address provider
Organization resolution of the Foundation Council
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resident agent resigns or becomes unavailable, appoint a substitute in a special council resolution and register the substitution with the Public Registry at the applicable tariff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National tax registration (RUC) and municipal notice of operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipality of Panama – Aviso de Operación window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, file the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) application and obtain the fiscal identification number. Simultaneously file the municipal Aviso de Operación to register the mail-order retail business under ISIC 4791 and obtain municipal operating standing.
required_dossiers: Public Registry inscription certificate
Foundation Charter excerpt translated into Spanish
Foundation Council resolution authorizing the commencement of retail operations
Lease contract or address consent for the operational premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI or municipality returns a query, resubmit the required Spanish notarized documents and pay any outstanding municipal revision tax; the Aviso is released immediately upon clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Facility fire safety, structural, and environmental clearance for pick/pack warehouse operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the foundation operates a physical fulfillment or warehouse location for cash-on-delivery mail-order retail, obtain a fire safety inspection certificate, a structural load certificate for storage racks from a registered Panamanian engineer, and an environmental categorization letter from MiAMBIENTE. MITRADEL verifies occupational safety for any hired staff.
required_dossiers: Building occupancy permit
Certified engineer's structural load assessment
Fire extinguisher maintenance records and evacuation plan
Solid waste handling commitment letter
List of personnel exposure controls for occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate identified fire or structural deficiencies and schedule a re-inspection within ten working days; for MiAMBIENTE, a revised activity classification may be requested with updated facility floor plans.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 mail-order retail; no sectorial industrial license is statutorily mandated. Reference authority for commercial promotion and trade facilitation: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industry-specific operating license; the entity operates under the municipal Aviso de Operación and DGI RUC registration. A commercial warehouse, if used, requires a complementary municipal occupancy permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 0 (Exempt) – no formal EIA report or registration is required for administrative and mail-order distribution activities without significant industrial emissions. MiAMBIENTE may issue a certificate of exception or a simplified environmental commitment letter.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater is generated. Sanitary discharges, if any, must conform to municipal sewer ordinances and generally maintain pH 6–9 and BOD5 below 100 mg/L. VOC emissions from packaging adhesives and printing must remain de minimis or be controlled with certified capture systems. Solid waste must be segregated, transported, and disposed of through licensed waste operators in accordance with MiAMBIENTE guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá after inspection of the warehouse or pick/pack premises; structural load certificate signed by a registered Panamanian engineer for racking systems; MITRADEL occupational hygiene and safety inspection for workplaces with employees; municipal certificate confirming the permitted commercial use of the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama City; online portal: Sede Electrónica Fiscal at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must first be inscribed in the Public Registry of Panama and maintain a resident agent. To obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), the foundation or its resident fiduciary representative submits to the DGI a sworn application, the registered foundation charter and bylaws, proof of the resident agent appointment, confirmation of the local address, and a declaration of the economic activities actually carried out. Where the PIF is exclusively an asset-holding or family-patrimony vehicle, no Panamanian-source income is declared; however, any taxable activity in Panama, including mail-order retail or e-commerce logistics, requires registration as an ITBMS responsible party before commencing operations. Non-resident PIFs generally use a local authorized representative with notarized power of attorney for RUC procurement and ongoing compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope (only Panamanian-source income is taxed; foreign-source income is exempt from Panamanian corporate income tax; the PIF itself does not have a separate per-se taxable classification and may remain non-commercial if its charter restricts activities to estate preservation and family patrimony)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a check-the-box election equivalent to the U.S. regime. A PIF may, through its foundation charter, elect a patrimony-only object, which reinforces its non-commercial, territorial-exempt status. No domestic hybrid mismatch election exists; the DGI applies substance-over-form and adjustment rules in accordance with the Panamanian Tax Code, CFC attribution rules, and applicable international information-exchange agreements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (transfer tax on movable goods and services; a value-added-style indirect tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis registration threshold applies to ITBMS; every person habitually transferring taxable movable goods or providing taxable services in Panama must obtain a RUC before commencing operations. A simplified 'pequeño contribuyente' regime may apply to small taxpayers, but it does not remove the obligation to register and report ITBMS where taxable commercial activities occur.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The DGI operates a mandatory fiscal invoicing regime through the Sede Electrónica Fiscal. Taxpayers enrolled as ITBMS responsible parties must issue invoices in electronic XML form or through DGI-authorized fiscal printer systems, transmit invoice data to the DGI through public web-service APIs, and obtain a digital reception acknowledgement and QR stamp prior to delivery. Invoice records must include the authorization folio, issuer RUC, rates, and cancellation status; real-time clearance obligations are progressively phased in by revenue band.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS at 0% applies to exports of movable goods when title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer and the goods physically depart Panama, evidenced by customs documentation. Services may be zero-rated when supplied to non-residents and effectively used, consumed, or exploited outside Panama. The zero-rating claim must be substantiated by an unbroken documentation chain proving physical export, foreign-payment receipt, and the non-resident status of the counterparty. Because Panama is a dollarized economy with no exchange-control regime, there is no statutory requirement or deadline to repatriate export proceeds into a particular Panamanian bank.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) accepted and stamped by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of goods from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of export settlement funds in USD
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA jointly cross-match export declarations, cargo manifests, freight bills, and banking records to detect fictitious zero-rated exports. A false export claim triggers immediate recharacterization of the sale as a taxable domestic supply, assessment of unpaid ITBMS at 7%, monthly interest for late payment, a 50% fraud surcharge under Article 717 of the Panamanian Tax Code, fines up to B/. 50,000, cancellation of fiscal authorization to issue invoices, and criminal prosecution for aggravated tax fraud which may result in imprisonment. The statute of limitations for retrospective clawback is generally six fiscal years from the date the tax return became due.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) acts as the primary banking and financial regulatory authority, while Banco Nacional de Panamá serves as the State's fiscal agent. Panama has no formal central bank; the effective monetary authority is the U.S. Federal Reserve due to full dollarization, and no dedicated foreign exchange control commission exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar (USD) is legal tender and circulates freely alongside the Panamanian balboa (PAB), which exists only as a coin. Capital and current account transactions are fully convertible with no surrender, approval, or import/export permit requirements for foreign exchange. Profit remittances to non-residents are unrestricted; however, income generated within Panamanian territory remains subject to territorial taxation and the applicable 10% dividend tax unless the payment is a return of invested capital or arises from a foreign source. No capital controls, restrictions on bank account funding, or withholding on principal repatriation exist.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Panama. Export receipts may be retained in USD or any foreign currency in offshore or domestic accounts without time-bound repatriation requirements. Panamanian customs and tax regulations require proper invoicing and BOI (Single Window) filing for statistical and tax purposes, but do not impose compulsory conversion or forced crediting to local bank accounts. For scope ISIC 4791 (mail-order retail with COD settlement), cash-on-delivery logistics remittances are treated as ordinary trade receivables and may be settled directly to the foundation's account without currency conversion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Panama does not license digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) as standalone 'bank-like' entities under a specific EMI statute; fintech services are governed by the General Banking Law (Decree Law 9 of 1998) and the Communications and Digital Technology Law (Law 31 of 2021). Airwallex, as a foreign licensed EMI, cannot operate a booking center in Panama without obtaining a SBP fintech authorization or partnering with a local bank. However, Airwallex-type rails may be used for downstream disbursement to logistics counterparties without establishing a local presence, provided funds flow through a Panamanian licensee or a correspondent settlement account. Direct onboarding of a Panamanian foundation as an Airwallex client is permissible when UBO identification and foundation documentation satisfy Airwallex's global compliance, but it does not replace a domestic Panamanian bank account for escrow or tax-sensitive funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted by Panamanian practice, but the SBP regulates that banks must apply a risk-based approach consistent with 'Conozca su Cliente' guidelines. In practice, Tier 1 banks require at least one appointed legal representative or ultimate beneficial owner to appear physically before a risk officer or to complete a notarized and apostilled power of attorney allowing the bank's relationship manager or a local attorney to sign the KYC declaration. Video-based iKYC interviews are increasingly accepted by private banks for low-risk entities, but for a Private Interest Foundation engaged in cross-border cash-on-delivery e-commerce (categorized as Medium-Risk Enhanced), the decisive requirement is measurable personal interaction: either an in-person interview at a Panamanian branch or a certified video call with documentary identity verification (passport, residence proof, and public registry background check). Directors are not subject to a nationwide physical-presence mandatory rule, but the bank's own compliance committee may impose an interview waiver only if the foundation maintains a Panama-licensed registered agent and the bank receives an opinion letter from a recognized compliance counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation (PIF) legal form with opaque protection of settlor and beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original Foundation Charter and Articles of Incorporation stamped by the Public Registry; certified copy of the Foundation's founder and beneficiary schedule (where disclosed); sworn declaration under penalty of perjury from the registered agent identifying the settlor, foundation council members, and protector (if any); supporting document of economic rationale (RUC or NIT tax ID, e-commerce licenses of logistics operators, source of funds letters). For enhanced due diligence, provide a Cayman Islands-style compliance certificate from the non-resident foundation council, plus a written attestation that the foundation is not used as a nominee shell.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-on-delivery (COD) trade flows with unknown local logistics operators and high volume of repeated small-value remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed logistics agency agreement; ISO 27001 or equivalent certification of the e-commerce platform; historical turnover projections with reconcilable transaction reports; list of 10 largest recipient logistics entities, each with valid RUC / national identity; anti-fraud compliance manual adopting the WEP (Watersoft, E-commerce and Payments) 2021 guidance; attestation from the payment processor (Airwallex or local enabling partner) showing that all COD collections are linked to a confirmed order and not merely person-to-person transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of bearer-style documentary rights or foreign foundation council members without a Panama supervisory nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Preventive measures under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Agreement 1-2022: provide the constitution of the foundation council naming at least three members, their passport copies, police clearance from their residence countries, and a commitment clause subjecting the foundation and council to SBP's inspection powers; bank-specific form (F-100 or equivalent) confirming that the foundation's legal address matches the registered agent and that the registered agent is licensed by the Attorney General's Office. If a protector has reserved powers, attach the protector's declaration of non-interference in banking matters and proof of the bank's consent waiver.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections for a Panamanian foundation should be routed through a clearing bank that is a member of the Panama Interbank Electronic Clearing House (ACH Panama) and the SWIFT network. The instruction must contain the foundation's account number, foundation full legal name, and a purpose code aligned with the Panamanian banking directive for capital contributions. For USD injections, use SWIFT MT103 with field 72 coded as '/REC/ Capital Contribution - Purchase of Foundation Assets' or '/INV/ Operating Funds Advanced by Founder' to prevent misinterpretation as taxable income. If the originating bank country is a FATF gray-listed jurisdiction, add the beneficiary's RUC (Régimen Único de Contribuyente) and the Panamanian registered agent's reference number. Verification step requires the receiving bank to issue an 'Acreditación de Fondos Externos' letter that includes the source of funds declaration, which must be retained for five years under the Joint Provision 1-2015.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for mail-order retail trade should be made using (1) SWIFT MT103 documentary payment for high-value logistics intermediaries, (2) commercial letters of credit (documentary credit under UCP 600) for purchase of merchandise with Incoterms 2020 (FCA or CIP) and port-city settlement, (3) ACH Panama wire or local transfer for same-day disbursement to registered logistics couriers; and (4) corporate procurement cards linked to a segregated collection account for COD controllers. Each MT103 must include an invoice reference and the phrase 'Trade Settlement - ISIC 4791' to avoid bank rejection due to ambiguous purpose. When the recipient is a local courier collecting cash on delivery, use the 'REMESA DETALLE' flag and require final account reconciliation, but do not send cash via wire; instead, instruct the carrier to deposit the COD proceeds into the foundation's account via a daily batch file transmitted by the logistics operator's bank. The clearing rail must maintain a four-hour T+0 gross settlement for local USD transfers; no T+1 conversion is applied.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: No Dominican-peso or central-bank NDF is required because Panama is fully dollarized; however, a standard USD/EUR or USD/CNH deliverable forward contract is permissible through SBP-regulated banking entities, with no requirement to obtain Panamanian Foreign Exchange Administration approval.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) with a licensed Panamanian bank or an international counterparty are permissible for hedging working capital credit obligations, provided the transaction is documented under ISDA and the bank assesses the foundation's non-investment-grade credit exposure.

Currency options (call/put USD against the relevant emerging-market currency) are permissible for hedging purchase-price risk on COD inventory, subject to the bank's internal product suitability rules for a special-purpose foundation; no local mandatory clearing through an exchange exists.

A multilateral spot contract denominated in Panamanian balboa or USD is not a separate hedging instrument; the foundation may use USD/USD synthetic forward transactions to manage interest-rate risk, but for the COD e-commerce model the most pragmatic structure is a 'firm-fix' FX agreement with the payment processor (Airwallex or similar) fixing the local currency collection rate for the 10-day COD clearing cycle.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise tax (Tasa Única Anual) return and payment for Private Interest Foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge plus 1% monthly default interest on the unpaid amount; failure to pay for two consecutive periods may result in publication of arrears, suspension of the RUC tax ID, and administrative strike-off of the foundation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual report (Informe Anual) and registry data confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the anniversary month of the foundation's inscription date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs registry tariff surcharges; the foundation is declared in arrears, restricted from issuing official certificates, and subject to suspension followed by cancellation after prolonged non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership (Beneficiario Final) confirmation and update filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) via the Beneficial Ownership Registry electronic platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually within the month corresponding to the foundation's registration anniversary, as scheduled by the DGI portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Law 254 of 2020 ranging from USD 1,000 to USD 100,000 depending on severity; repeated non-confirmation may trigger suspension of legal capacity, registry strike-off, and reporting to the Financial Analysis Unit.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Private Interest Foundation is not generally required to publish audited financial statements; however, when it exercises commercial or economic activities in Panama, an independent audit is mandatory if annual gross income exceeds USD 750,000 or total assets exceed USD 3,000,000, per Law 65 of 2005 and Executive Decree 17 of 2019.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as endorsed by the Panamanian College of Public Accountants for audited entities; IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para PYMES) permitted for non-public-interest entities; books may be kept in United States dollars, the official legal tender of Panama.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 254 of 2020, the Foundation Council must maintain a current register of founders, council members, and beneficiaries and certify it through an annual confirmation filed on the DGI platform during the foundation's anniversary month; any transfer of foundation capital or substitution of beneficiaries during the year must be reported to the DGI within 30 days of the formal amendment and reflected in the next annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (Registro de Consejeros)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Corporation Income Tax, ISR – Impuesto sobre la Renta)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation excludes all foreign-source income. Panamanian free trade zones and special economic zones may grant 10- to 15-year CIT exemptions on qualifying export activity. PIFs engaged solely in passive asset holding or foreign-investment activities generally have no Panamanian-source taxable income and therefore no effective CIT. No general statutory tax holiday is available for a standard PIF unless it activates a licensed activity under specific promotion laws (e.g., tourism, reforestation, SEM).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 120 (Declaración Jurada de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) - Sede Electrónica DGI, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá; filing is mandatory via electronic portal at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending 31 December, the return must be filed between 1 March and 31 March of the following year, with the precise final date determined by the RUC/NIT last digit. For other fiscal year-ends, the return is due no later than the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end. Quarterly advance instalments are required for taxpayers with previous-year taxable income above the threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC/NIT, legal name, fiscal address, and registered agent identifier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIFs must enter their Panamanian RUC/NIT and registered agent reference; non-resident status of beneficiaries is noted in the declarations section, not here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from Panamanian-source or territorially taxable activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs engaged in foreign commerce must report only Panamanian-source income; foreign-source revenue is excluded under the territorial principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions, costs, expenses, and depreciation attributable to Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be proportionate to Panamanian-source income; expenses paid to related non-resident parties require transfer pricing disclosure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and loss carryforwards (maximum five years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIFs claiming reduced treaty relief must attach documentation to arrive at correct net taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable CIT rate applied to net taxable income (standard 25%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs subject to tax at source do not complete Box 5 unless they have a permanent establishment or taxed activity in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting corporation income tax after applying the rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a DTA limits Panama's taxing right, the reduced rate is entered only after formal approval from DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Pagos a Cuenta y Retenciones
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, quarterly instalments, withholding tax credits, and tax credits from incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs must claim foreign tax credits only if permitted under tax treaty provisions; attach TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Impuesto a Pagar o Saldo a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax due or refund balance after credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If claiming a refund, the PIF must have a Panamanian bank account and submit to DGI audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate annual related-party transaction schedule with associated persons, amounts, and methodology.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs with cross-border related-party transactions exceeding threshold must file the transfer pricing annex even if no Panamanian tax is due.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a surcharge of 1% per month on the unpaid tax up to a maximum of 10%, plus interest at statutory rates. Flat penalties for failure to file or for filing erroneous returns range from USD 100 to USD 500, with higher fines for intentional understatement. Failure to file the transfer pricing annex may trigger an additional penalty of up to 1% of related-party transaction value. Criminal sanctions apply for fraudulent non-filing or deliberate evasion, including imprisonment of up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% statutory withholding on dividends distributed from Panamanian taxable profits, applied at the time of distribution to both residents and non-residents, unless the distributing company is in a regime with specific exemption. Dividends sourced from foreign-source income are outside the territorial system and generally not subject to Panamanian WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident beneficiary must submit a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty country, together with a completed Formularia de Solicitud de Exención/ Aplicación de Convenio ante la DGI. The withholding agent must file the form and retain supporting documents for five years. Relief is granted only upon prior administrative approval by the Tax Office (Dirección General de Ingresos); for tax treaties, DGI may require the beneficiary to demonstrate beneficial ownership and economic substance. Rejection triggers standard 5% WHT plus interest if not timely applied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 12.5% WHT on Panamanian-source royalty payments to non-residents; treaty rates typically 5-10% depending on IP type and DTA. Interest: statutory 12.5% WHT on Panamanian-source interest paid to non-residents, unless paid to a foreign bank under qualifying loan provisions or reduced to 5-10% under an applicable tax treaty; treaty relief requires the same TRC submission.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 1,000,000 (equivalent to USD 1,000,000) aggregate annual value of related-party transactions, per DGI transfer pricing regulations; lower de minimis thresholds may apply to specific transaction types.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama Law 52 of 2019 (as amended) introduces Economic Substance Regulations for entities carrying on 'relevant activities' – banking, financing, distribution, shipping, and IP-holding – within Panama. PIFs passively holding assets or carrying out cash-on-delivery e-commerce intermediation must maintain adequate staff, premises, and local strategic management if they claim territorial benefits or treaty access. Annual ESR reporting is mandatory through the DGI online portal; failure to demonstrate substance can lead to administrative sanctions up to PAB 2,000,000 and is grounds for exchanging information under international tax transparency standards.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Panamanian-source income, inflating deductions, or submitting a false Formulario 120 to suppress tax liability; also includes failure to disclose beneficial owners in the annual registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalties: fine of up to 10 times the evaded tax, plus statutory interest, and imprisonment of 3-5 years. Administrative penalty: up to USD 50,000 for fraudulent misrepresentation. DGI may re-audit open years and assess tax deficiency with a 20% surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, foundation council members, and fiduciary agents are jointly and severally liable for fraud, and may face civil restitution, attachment of personal assets, travel bans, and imprisonment in addition to corporate sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF without any physical presence, beneficial owner identification, or economic substance while claiming tax-resident benefits, foreign-source income exclusions, or treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 52 of 2019, penalties range from USD 50,000 to USD 2,000,000 for substance violations; failure to file ESR returns attracts daily fines and the entity may be struck off the registry. In DTA abuse cases, the competent authority can deny treaty benefits and re-characterise all income as Panamanian-source, resulting in 25% CIT and 12.5% WHT penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Council members who knowingly approve baseless substance declarations can be fined personally up to USD 500,000 and banned from acting as a director or registered agent in Panama for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct customer due diligence on beneficiaries, maintaining opaque cash-on-delivery settlement trails with anonymous remitters, or failing to report suspicious transactions to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Severe administrative fines up to USD 5,000,000 for institutions, and individual fines up to USD 1,000,000; criminal money-laundering conviction carries imprisonment up to 12 years and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and officers face criminal prosecution for AML violations, including imprisonment, civil forfeiture of personal assets, travel bans, and professional disqualification. The corporate veil may be pierced where the foundation is used as an instrument of fraud.
